Low/falling BG or clinical signs: prompt DVM review of glucose support and insulin. Symptomatic/severe hypoglycemia requires immediate treatment. More info / Other charts ↓ · Sources ↓

Best use: Fixed-rate DKA insulin with dextrose support as needed; follow glucose, ketones, hydration and electrolytes. Veterinary sources.

Regular insulin IV CRI · Fixed-rate DKA default: 0.1 U/kg/hr for dogs and cats. Confirm hydration, potassium, glucose monitoring and dextrose support before starting. No automatic titration or stop rule.

Fixed-rate DKA preparation

Alternative dosing presets
Stock concentration · locked by default

Assumed U-100 regular insulin; verify vial. Tiny stock volumes are shown with extra precision: use a validated measuring/dilution method when needed. Account for line adsorption/priming under your insulin protocol; displayed duration is nominal before priming/discard. Run time sets preparation quantity, not how long DKA should be treated.

Fixed-rate protocol: support glucose with dextrose as needed while treating ketosis; monitor BG frequently and follow the treating veterinarian’s adjustment/hold criteria if glucose falls too low. Monitor potassium, phosphorus, hydration and ketones. Do not stop insulin solely because glucose normalizes. The 0.045 feline alternative is a variable-rate starting approach, not the fixed-rate default. Dose evidence & protocol limits. Dextrose preparation.

Worked math

More info / Other charts

BG → dextrose support · fixed-rate DKA

Reference target: 180–270 mg/dL. Combined clinical reference adapted from the fixed-rate literature and your workbook; this exact combined chart has not been prospectively validated. Insulin and glucose-support decisions remain clinician-directed.

BG · mg/dLDextrose / action
≥270Dextrose may not yet be required. Review the BG trend and existing supplementation.
180 to <2705% dextrose starting solution in the fixed-rate reference; titrate glucose delivery toward the selected BG target.
100 to <180Below target: reassess promptly and increase glucose support as prescribed. Consider a higher concentration when fluid volume limits delivery. Insulin reduction or a temporary hold remains an option; Gant’s protocol used a hold threshold of <126 mg/dL.
<100Immediate DVM review. Consider increasing dextrose to 7.5–10% with appropriate vascular access; consider central access for ongoing concentrated support. Review insulin and consider temporary reduction/hold. Consider NG nutrition ± clinician-prescribed carbohydrate supplementation as an adjunct when appropriate.
Workbook tip · 2.5% dextrose

Dextrose support—including 2.5% when sufficient—can help support continued prescribed insulin for ketone clearance. Your workbook lists 2.5% for BG 250–299 and 150–249 mg/dL. Use the prescribed concentration and mL/hr together to provide the required glucose; 2.5% is an option, not an automatic fixed-rate dose rule.

Symptomatic or severe hypoglycemia requires immediate treatment and insulin reassessment under the hypoglycemia protocol. Tube placement or enteral support must not delay correction. NG support is adjunctive nutrition, not a validated equivalent substitute for IV glucose rescue.

Measure BG frequently and after treatment changes under the prescribed protocol. The same dextrose % at different fluid rates delivers different glucose doses. Prepare prescribed dextrose concentration → · Sources below ↓

Sources

  1. Gant, Barfield & Florey · JVECC 2024 · Fixed- versus variable-rate insulin in canine/feline DKAPrimary fixed-rate study: methods deliver 0.1 U/kg/hr; 5% dextrose below BG 270, with target 180–270. Temporary hold below 126. Abstract prints 0.01, inconsistent with methods/results; see detailed source notes.
  2. Igor Yankin, DACVECC · VetEmCrit · DKA insulin protocol reviewPractical three-bag explanation; higher dextrose concentrations and central-access considerations.
  3. VetEmCrit · Fixed-rate DKA calculator and printable order chart
  4. AAHA 2026 · Canine diabetic ketoacidosisManagement context and glucose support; not the source of this exact combined chart.
  5. AAHA 2026 · Feline DKA and euglycemic DKAIncludes escalation of dextrose support for eDKA; these recommendations are not automatically generalized to every DKA patient.
  6. Elke Rudloff · JFMS 2017 · Feline DKA: recognition and essential treatmentTraditional insulin protocol, glucose monitoring, temporary insulin hold and NG nutritional support. Does not establish NG dextrose as equivalent to IV glucose rescue.
  7. Anderson, Rondeau & Hess · JVIM 2019 · Lispro and regular insulin in feline DKAInitial 0.09 U/kg/hr in both treatment groups; compares insulin products rather than starting-dose superiority.
  8. Claus et al. · JVECC 2010 · Regular insulin infusion doses in 29 catsRetrospective prescribed-dose comparison; delivered doses were reduced by variable-rate adjustments.
  9. Uploaded workbook · DKA H37:K43 · Original BG/dextrose chart and adaptation recordSource of the prior 2.5% tip and <100 higher-concentration/feeding considerations. Main quick-reference bands were subsequently selected by the site owner.
